title: Reading notes: LLM inference optimizations & conference takeaways (Miguel Alvarez)
summary: Quick notes on recent papers, blogs, and experiments related to production inference: KV cache strategies, batching tradeoffs, quantization profiles, and a few conference takeaways. Focused on actionable ideas to prototype in the runtime over the next quarter.
notes: ICLR/NeurIPS sweep (Feb 2026): flash attention improvements + kernel-level scheduling; adaptive kernel selection based on seq-len distributions looks promising to reduce tail latency.

KV-cache compaction: periodically compact older KV entries when session prefix probability is low. Reported ~20% memory reduction with <1% perplexity change on long-context tasks. Candidate for Dedicated long-chat workloads.

Continuous batching vs request coalescing: for low-QPS interactive traffic, continuous batching (short time-window batching) improves GPU utilization but adds jitter. Need p95 impact measurements for 7B/13B at RTTs we see (50-200ms).
Quantization: 4-bit APC/QLoRA-style profiles can give up to 2x throughput in blogs, but quality varies by prompt. Prioritize controlled evals on reranking and embeddings before production rollouts.
Routing/cascades: simple small->big cascade with calibrated confidence can cut cost for many prompts. Suggest prototyping as an experiment in Redwood Optimize with per-route rollout controls.
Local benchmarks: 7B fp16 on A100, seq=512: avg token latency ~12ms without flash optimizations; with flash kernels down to ~7-8ms. Batch=1 p99 improved ~30% after kernel tuning.
Memory experiments: compacting KV for sessions >2048 tokens saved ~18% GPU memory on test traces. Validate with mixed-session workloads at scale.

ICLR talk highlights: operationalizing evals — emphasis on dataset-driven regression detection (prompt-based evals) and linking regressions to model/quantization changes. Aligns with our rollout + eval strategy.
Telemetry note: add per-route metric for model-variant escalations (count how often cascade escalates to bigger model). Important for cost/quality analysis.
Open question: frequency of kernel recompilation vs runtime heuristics. Recompilation yields best perf but is heavy for private/on-prem customers.
Implementation constraint: private deployments often run older CUDA stacks; plan fallback execution paths (degraded perf) and detect kernel availability at runtime.
User-facing tradeoff: latency-sensitive chat routes should target <50ms token latency p95; batch workloads should maximize throughput and cost efficiency.
